# Phase directive — «Key after a resize» (Epoch 4, viola-0.2.0; the head entry at `a32f6ef6`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped. A fact the
plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

The operator is AWAY (asleep; no dialog reaches him and nobody else gives a live-start cap): raise
NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the
options in order with each one's cost, the recommendation marked) and the step stops there, saying so. A technical
fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start and reads nothing of the
operator's real `~/.claude*`.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-21T23:30Z — cite them as this directive's

- A bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.330 (mise `latest`), and THIS session runs it; 2.1.328 stands installed by
  path. The pinned product (the release build of `a59da9da`) holds none of the last seven mends and is untouched
  until its re-pin.
- The tree at `a32f6ef6` holds 29 relied ledger rows; `fixtures/claude/` holds six version folders, ONE of them
  stamped (2.1.328, 33 files); `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE` and the rig's `MB` arm exist since the last chunk.
- The entry as the route holds it: «whether real `claude` on Linux loses a key typed right after a resize,
  measured; fixed if it does». Its carries: the Epoch 4 boundary's re-read of the advisory ignores (the
  operator's, at the boundary — not this chunk's work); the paste's missing time bound (one blocking PTY write
  in `viola-pty`'s pump, a finding of the last chunk; its own route entry waits for the operator's word); the
  rehearsal red, acted on only at its next red.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `a32f6ef6`, nothing wider. Every carry is disposed
   by name in the plan: the boundary carry is named as the boundary's; the paste carry is taken ONLY if this
   entry's own change opens that write path, and then as a fork of the block — folding it is not yours to decide.
2. **What can be told with NO start comes first.** At P3, from the tree, the masters, the store's history of the
   earlier chunks that met a lost key, and the installed 2.1.328 and 2.1.330 bundles read as strings, say:
   - where the claim comes from — which earlier chunk, test or report recorded a key lost after a resize, on
     which OS and CLI version, and what was read there (a recorded fact, or a hypothesis carried since);
   - what viola does around a resize today: who sends the window-size change, what is written to the PTY after
     it and when, every wait or settle bound in that path, and which tests and fake-agent behaviours hold it;
   - what the CLI does on a resize as its strings read it (a redraw, an input-mode reset, a debounce) — a
     READING, never a measurement;
   - what «measured» must mean for the row to be honest, and the cheapest live start that tells it: which
     process, the pty's sizes before and after, WHICH key bytes are typed and how long after the resize (the
     delays tried), into what state of the CLI (the empty input box, never a dialog), what is read to tell a
     lost key from a kept one (a screen literal's presence, viola's own events — a closed word, never a text),
     how many repetitions make a reading and what a mixed reading means, under which home and config;
   - what «fixed if it does» would be, as options priced before any start (a settle wait after a resize, a
     read-back and one re-type, a refusal) and which rows each would move — decided only AFTER the reading.
3. **A key typed into a real CLI by a rig is the operator's word per chunk, beside the cap.** Say every byte,
   and the state it is typed into; the rig's STOP is standing. Nothing is typed into a dialog. Whatever the rig
   newly reads, writes or spawns is a widening he has NOT seen — say it whole, with what is kept and where, and
   the proof that no screen text reaches a file, stamp, fixture or log. Before promising what a kept frame or a
   recorded payload holds, say what the CLI ITSELF puts on that screen (his status line, a path, an account
   word): a frame is kept locally and never lands.
4. **Every master row whose words the change reaches: search ALL seven masters before the block is written**
   (the resize path, the keys viola writes and their waits, `send`'s gate and its confirmation, time bounds and
   who waits, the live rig's rows, the wheel) and name EVERY reached row, with the ones read as not reached
   beside them. A widening is said as one HERE, whole; a row found reached AFTER the block is a fork of its own.
   A cell that cannot hold a new member under its bound is said in the block, not at the wrap.
5. **At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md` — and the phase then HOLDS, perhaps for
   hours:** your window; what was read with no start and what only a start can tell; the answer path
   recommended and the ones set aside, each with how it fails; every reached master row; every live start's
   SHAPE before the count — processes, every byte typed and into what, every dialog raised and how it is
   answered, the stop, every file written and where, under WHICH home; for each start a predicate its reading
   can FAIL, the red reading named; what each start READS and from WHERE; whether a typed key moves the wheel;
   which versions are measured; the capability's concretized claim and what «verified» would rest on; a
   recommended cap and what one spare would be for; whether one implement window holds it. The cap, any key or
   byte into a CLI, any widening, what «verified» rests on and any read or write under his real home are the
   operator's: the block WAITS. If the block holds NO fork of his, say so in its first line.
6. **For every capped start, name what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree** (a kept stamp, a kept
   dir, a scratch, a runtime dir — the kept `HF`/`HG`/`XS`/`XS-2` products among them), each with a no-start
   gate entry right before the start, placed so a round resumed at one entry still fires it; a start whose
   product is kept gets an entry that reads it AFTER.
7. One ledger, one count: `--cap` is the RUNNING total of base starts in the ledger file. A census entry after
   the LAST live leg is keyed to the operator leg.
8. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases AND building the whole workspace where the
   case needs a root binary; the bound that applies is the entry's own timeout key, ids within 16 characters.
   Every filter term of a gate entry SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag. An expect atom must be able
   to fail; a word that may honestly read two ways is a READING recorded, not a failing atom; an after-read of
   state OTHER actors move is keyed to the round leg. A control's id is 1–16 characters. A test that skips prints its reason. The plan names operator entries by their run text.
9. Before a live round the host is read (`hostwatch.py read --last 15`): a CONTENDED reading with a NEIGHBOUR
   named stops and is re-read, never retried into. The token window is the rig's own check, never a hand read; a
   start refused for it is uncounted — stop and say so.
10. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned
    user home. Read `df` before a whole rebuild.
11. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop
    and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop where you are.
12. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start; remove no scratch
    clone by a recursive delete — name it on the card instead. An entry that asserts a state a LATER step of the
    same plan ends is keyed to the round leg; the round's span holds round and live entries only, and the whole-round dry-run is shown on the card. Never write that the rig refuses a condition without the line that
    refuses it.
13. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the union or its standing
    list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` /
    `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

- **Harness rules consulted:** `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` — read whole (81 lines, `## Session Additions` included); the additions that bind a live leg here: 2026-10-10 (put the stamped version's install dir first on the rig's `PATH`, read `claude --version` by path; re-read `mise ls claude` at the proof), 2026-10-20 (read the build's hash right before a start), 2026-11-17 (a `mise` install holds `<version dir>/claude`, no `bin/`), 2026-11-18 (the token window is the rig's own check), 2026-11-19 (an expect asserts a reading that can fail, never `unread` / `none`), 2026-11-20 (a non-leg entry reading a round's file is keyed to the round leg).
- **Platform issues consulted:** none — no runner-only bullet (CI on `a32f6ef6` green 7/7) and no CI-reading entry outside the operator leg.

- **External inputs:** `inputs#I1` — the phase directive: no live start this phase, nothing read under the operator's real `~/.claude*`, the bundles read as strings only, P3 ends with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`, the host facts measured by the overseer 2026-11-21T23:30Z.

- `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` (1-240, 760-880) — `RESIZE_EVERY` 250 ms (`:13`): the pump POLLS the host size every 250 ms in its main loop (`:185-191`) and calls `pty.resize` on a change against the spawn size (`:166`, `:189`); no SIGWINCH handler. `PasteHandle::paste` (`:72-89`) is one bracketed `write_all` + flush under the shared input lock; the human copy thread writes each chunk under the same lock (`HumanInput`, `:92-108`). Nothing orders a key or a paste against a resize: the resize runs on the pump's main thread, the human copy and the paste on others.

- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` (1-300, 420-470, 600-960) — `PortablePty::resize` (`:186-191`, span `pty.resize`) → portable-pty `MasterPty::resize` (TIOCSWINSZ on the master). `host_size` reads `TIOCGWINSZ` on stdout (`:254-264`). The real-PTY tests: `spawn_runs_…_a_resize_…` waits for the child's `size 120x40` before its key (`:850-880`); `spawn_delivers_a_key_written_right_after_a_resize_to_a_child_not_yet_reading` (`:883-903`) writes `y` right after `resize` returned on Linux openpty, the child held out of its read 750 ms (`CHILD_HOLD`, `:286`), and asserts `byte 79 size=120x40`; `spawn_reports_a_resize_to_a_child_that_reads_no_key` (`:906-922`). The comment over `CHILD_WITHIN` (`:614`) still names «the nextest `mutants` profile's 10 s kill».

- `src/cmd/run.rs` (600-665) — `pump_child`: the `host_size` closure offers every read size to the gate's feed (`sizes.size(size)`, `:643-648`) BEFORE the pump compares and resizes, so the gate's screen model is rebuilt on the same poll that resizes the child.
- `src/run/gate.rs` (1-120) — `Model::resize` (`:53-61`): a new size rebuilds the screen blank (`Screen::resize`), clears poison, and resets `last_fed` to now.

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` (1-30, 300-410) — `QUIET_PERIOD` 300 ms, `GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s; `Screen::resize` (`:336-341`) builds a fresh parser and resets `last_fed`; `verdict` (`:369-401`): a blank screen after a resize is not quiet for 300 ms, then on a verified CLI waits for the input box rows to be redrawn, up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT`.

- `src/run/send.rs` (60-175) — `send_through`: `gate.wait_ready` (`:136`), then under the flight lock the second wheel and turn reads, `send-issued`, and the paste (`:144-170`). Nothing between the gate's `Ready` and the `write_all` re-reads the size: a resize polled in that window reaches the child just before or during the paste.
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` (1110-1135) — the `size` receipt watcher polls `host_size` on the control cadence; the fake agent keeps every key byte; nothing in it drops input on a resize.

- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs` (60-95) — `plain()`: 0x7f truncates the prompt to its last char boundary (`:73-85`), under «DEL erases the prompt's last character, as the live CLI's input box does».
- `tests/tui_pty_seam.rs` (50-90) — `pty_resize_reaches_the_child`, `pty_resize_reaches_a_child_that_reads_no_key`: the fake agent's `size` receipt with no key after the resize.

The rig's child runs on `viola_pty::spawn` (`:866`), so `PortablePty::resize` is at hand.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs` (1-80) — the closed key set `Down · Enter · X · Del`; the argv grant `trust` / `box`; refusal words `key-not-granted` · `key-not-ready` · `key-write-failed`.

data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; rust plane)

body: - **resize** (`callee_kind = 'fn'`) — 22 call sites (`tree-query-2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize.json`, query 1): product callers `pump/pump_open()` `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:188`, `run/gate/start()` `src/run/gate.rs:206` (the feed thread), `Model::resize` `src/run/gate.rs:59`, verify's `SharedPty::resize` `src/cmd/verify/typed/pty.rs:63`; the rest tests (`viola-pty` 4, `screen.rs` 3, `gate.rs` 3, `tests/tui_pty_seam.rs` 2, `tests/tui_passthrough.rs:134`, `tests/tui_wheel.rs:229`, `tests/support/home.rs:1023`, `tests/support/outer_pty.rs:108`, `src/cmd/run.rs:1375`, `src/cmd/verify/typed/pty.rs:440`). No rig caller.

- **paste** (`callee_file LIKE '%pump.rs'`) — 6 call sites (query 2): `cmd/run/pump_child()` `src/cmd/run.rs:640` (the send attach), verify's `Run::paste_text()` `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:181`, four `pump.rs` tests.

- **pump_with_paste** — 5 call sites (query 3): `pump()` `pump.rs:121`, `pump_child` `src/cmd/run.rs:649`, verify's `Run::spawn()` `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:151`, the `rig()` test helper, the crate re-export.
- Meaning: the measuring branch reaches no product symbol; a fix on the driver's side reaches `src/run/send.rs` / `src/run/gate.rs` (and through them `src/cmd/run.rs`), never `viola-pty`'s write.

- **The claim's origin is a Windows measurement, never a Linux one** (`doc:2026-09-29-h2-conpty-resize-probe/report`; gotchas.md:107-110): 13/200 on the windows-2025 runner's inbox ConPTY with a Rust test child; a sideloaded ConPTY read 0/200 against inbox 14/200 in one run (chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty, arch-history item 4); the real `claude` was never read on any OS. The owner chain: «First live test and self-drive» → «Windows-only live measurements» → the `another-os` residuals → this entry (census C-288 / C-729, 2026-11-08). A HYPOTHESIS carried since, not a recorded Linux fact.

- **On Linux openpty, the seam already delivers a key written right after a resize to a Rust child** — `spawn_delivers_a_key_written_right_after_a_resize_to_a_child_not_yet_reading` (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:886`) passes on CI's one `ubuntu-latest` leg (ci#44960846431 green): the key waits in the kernel tty buffer through the resize. What remains open is the CLI's own handling above the kernel.

- **viola's resize is polled, not signalled**: `RESIZE_EVERY` 250 ms (`pump.rs:13`). A human key typed into `viola run` right after a host resize reaches the child BEFORE the child's own resize, by up to 250 ms; the child sees «a key right after its resize» only for a key typed about one poll after the host's resize, or for a driver paste racing the poll.

- **The driver's send is gated on a redraw after a resize**: the size offered to the feed rebuilds the gate's screen blank (`gate.rs:53-61`, `screen.rs:336`), so a send whose gate wait spans the resize waits `QUIET_PERIOD` and, on a verified CLI, the redrawn input box. The window left: a resize polled after the gate returned `Ready` and before the paste's `write_all` (`send.rs:136` → `:166`).

- **A lost or cut paste is never presumed delivered**: the confirmation needs the submitted prompt to equal the typed text, or that text less a trailing whitespace run (`decision/send-confirmation-trailing-trim-match`); a leading byte lost reads `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` after `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` 10 s — but the CLI may already have run the cut prompt as a turn (the paste's Enter is its last byte).

data.head: ### A. The arm `KR` (tests S1–S4; security S1, S3; arch S1, S2, S5)

body:
1. **The grant** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs`:
   - `Grant` gains `resize: bool`, set by the argv word `resize` (`--grant box,resize`); any other word still refuses
     the grant whole. A resize is no key: the closed `Key` set stays `Down · Enter · X · Del`.
   - `Keys` gains `may_resize()`, true only under that grant.
   - The X and DEL a round types after its resize go through the existing `type_key` with the frame read BEFORE the
     resize as its `on` (the box read up and empty there, `inputs#I2` item 3). No other readiness rule is added.
   - Inline cases (keeps tests S3, S4): `box,resize` grants both; `resize` alone grants no X; an unknown word refuses;
     `may_resize` is false under `box`.

2. **The model's resize** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs`:
   - `Model::resize(rows, cols)` sets the parser's screen size in place (vt100 0.16.2 `Screen::set_size`, which keeps
     the cells as a terminal does; `~/.cargo/registry/src/*/vt100-0.16.2/src/screen.rs:88`) and updates `cols`.
   - A poisoned model stays poisoned.
   - Inline cases: a fed box row reads `box: up` after a resize to 180×40 and back; a poisoned model reads `poisoned`
     after one.

3. **The round's pure parts** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`, beside `attr_counts` (no clock read, no I/O):
   - `KR_ROUNDS` = 12.
   - `kr_delay(n)` → 0, 20 or 100 ms, interleaved `0 · 20 · 100` from round 1, four each.
   - `kr_size(n)` → 180×40 on odd rounds, 210×45 (the rig's `screen::COLS` × `screen::ROWS`) on even ones, so the width
     changes every round.
   - `kr_round_word(typed, hint, first, again)` → `kept` when `first` equals the typed word, or `again` (the re-read
     after a further settle, `Some` only when `first` equals the hint word) does; `lost` when both equal the hint word;
     else `unread`.
   - `kr_reading(kept, lost, unread)` → `kept` at 12 kept; `lost` at one lost or more; else `unverified`.
   - Inline cases produce every word: `kept`, `kept` late (`again` the typed word), `lost`, `unread` (an
     `unread (no-box)` first), and the three readings; the schedule's 4·4·4 count and the size alternation.

4. **The arm** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`:
   - `Arm::KR`, word `kr`; live labels `KR` · `KR8` and spares `KR-2` · `KR8-2` in `of_label` (`ledger::admit`'s
     `-2` rule).
   - Seeds as `HB`: `has_vhome` false, `verify_seed` false, `marker_seed` true, `trusted` true, `wrapped` None, pty
     the rig's 210×45.
   - `Session` gains `resize(size)`, which calls `PortablePty::resize` on its own pty (`viola_pty::Pty::resize`), then
     `Model::resize`.
   - `arm_kr`, in this order:
     1. Without `may_resize` and the `box` grant: no key, `refused: grant`.
     2. The first frame is read (`first_frame`, `record_reading`). Trust shown, a modal, or no box: no key, `refused:
        shape` (as `arm_hb`).
     3. **The control:** settle until the box reads up; type `x` on that frame; settle; keep `after-x`; read
        `box_attr` as the typed word; type DEL; settle; keep `after-del`; read `box_attr` as the hint word. Typed equal
        to hint → `control: confounded`, no round. Else `control: told-apart`.
     4. **Each round n = 1…12:**
        1. Settle until the box reads up; read `box_attr`. Not the hint word → `dirty-box` at round n, and the arm
           stops.
        2. Take that reading as the frame the keys are checked on, then `session.resize(kr_size(n))`.
        3. Pump output for `kr_delay(n)` (the session's own pump, never a bare sleep: the delay is a bound on reading,
           not a wait on the child).
        4. Type `x` on the pre-resize frame; settle; keep `kr-x`; read `box_attr` (`first`). If it is the hint word,
           settle again and read it once more (`again`). Then `kr_round_word`.
        5. Type DEL; settle; keep `kr-del`.
     5. A key the grant refuses (`key-not-ready` on a modal) ends the arm with that round `unread`.
   - **Summary keys** (`ledger::print_summary`, the ledger's summary line and the evidence; closed words and counts
     only, never screen text — security S3): `keys` (the `Keys::summary` word, `x 13, del 13` on a whole start),
     `box`, `modal`, `control`, `rounds` (rounds run), `kept` · `lost` · `unread` (each `{k}/12`), `kept-0ms` ·
     `kept-20ms` · `kept-100ms` (each `{k}/4`), `lost-at` (the delays a `lost` fell on, comma-joined, or `none`),
     `kr-reading` (`kept` · `lost` · `unverified`), `sizes` (`210x45-180x40`), `dirty-box` (`none` or the round), then
     the rig's own (`census`, `credentials`, `scratch`, `user-config`).
   - **`finish`'s whole-start rule:** a start is whole when the rig's own rule holds, `control` reads `told-apart`,
     `rounds` reads 12 and `kr-reading` is not `unverified`. So a `lost` reading still ends a whole start (exit 0): it
     is the measurement, judged by the round's reading entries, never the rig's red.
   - `parse`, `word`, `of_label`, the label and arm tables' cases, and the module doc gain the arm.

5. **The CLI** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`: `kr` among `rehearse`'s words; `KR` · `KR8` (and
   spares) in `live`'s doc line, with one sentence: a plain `claude` whose own pty the rig resizes 12 times, one `x` and
   one DEL after each resize, no send.

6. **The rehearsals** — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`, in `rig_rehearsal_hb_…`'s shape, over the fake agent
   (`case.child(true, &[])`, `--screens`). Keeps tests S1–S4; security S1, S3.
   - `rig_rehearsal_kr_reads_each_key_kept_after_its_own_resize` (`--grant box,resize`):
     - exit 0;
     - `arm: kr`, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `control: told-apart`, `rounds: 12`, `kept: 12/12`, `lost: 0/12`,
       `kr-reading: kept`, `dirty-box: none`;
     - the fake agent's receipt holds a `size` line for 180×40 and one for 210×45 (the resize reached the child), and
       no `prompt` line (no send);
     - keys read from the rig's own `keys` word, never from the receipt (`test-plan ·
       decision/rig-no-key-read-from-keys-word`);
     - `assert_torn_down`.
   - `rig_rehearsal_kr_without_the_resize_grant_types_nothing` (`--grant box`): `refused: grant`, `keys: none`, no
     `size` receipt past the start's own, torn down.
   - The fake agent keeps every byte through a resize, so a red here is the arm's own.

title: B. The round — fired by implement under the cap, `leg` entries (`inputs#I2` items 2, 5, 7, 9)

data.head: ### B. The round — fired by implement under the cap, `leg` entries (`inputs#I2` items 2, 5, 7, 9)

body:
7. **Entries 6–19, in order:**
   - the host read, the two installs by path, `mise ls`, the census, the rig's build and its hash;
   - the kept products' sha set and the live home's stamp sha, read before the round;
   - `KR` (`--cap 1`), then `KR8` (`--cap 2`), each `--spare 1`, on one ledger
     `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize/evidence/kr-starts.ndjson`;
   - the two after-reads, then the two readings.

   **The two starts are ordered independent** (`inputs#I2` item 7): each version's reading is its own. A `lost` on `KR`
   is not a rig red, so `KR8` still runs; the reading entries 18–19 come last, and the first red among them stops the
   round there.

   A start that exits 1 (`refused shape`, `confounded`, `dirty-box`, `unverified`, the token window, a host stall) stops
   the round at its own entry. Its ledger line is read first; the spare (`KR-2` or `KR8-2`) is then a plan revision's
   entry on the overseer's word, never a re-fire of the base entry. A `lost` is never a spare's. A third base start is
   the operator's. On an account-limit refusal implement stops where it is (`inputs#I1` item 11).

8. **After the span:** the census keyed `operator` (entry 20). Then the ledger's two summaries read back, closed words
   and counts only (entry 21, report-only), copied by implement into
   `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize/evidence/live-round.md` from those typed fields alone. No kept
   frame is read into that file, a message, a log or the tree (`inputs#I2` item 6).

9. The whole integration layer, the smoke, `pre-push`, hygiene (which reads the evidence dir), the push and CI
   (entries 22–29).
- none
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs` — `Grant.resize`, the `resize` word, `Keys::may_resize`, the grant cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs` — `Model::resize`, its cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `Arm::KR`, its labels and seeds, `Session::resize`, the round's pure parts, `arm_kr`, the summary keys, `finish`'s rule, the table cases, the module doc
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — `kr` and `KR` · `KR8` in the doc lines
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the two `KR` rehearsals
**The order.**

- Phase A: the formatter, the linter, the rig library cases, the `KR` rehearsals through the integration layer (which
  builds the root binaries they spawn), and the workspace unit layer.

- The round: entries 6–19, `round` and `live` entries ONLY (`inputs#I2` item 9). Its after-reads of state other actors
  move are keyed to the round.

- After the span: the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole integration layer and
  the operator pass.
**What is not run, and why.**
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10).
- No `--e2e` layer: no MCP, contract or path surface is touched; the rig is test-only.
- No release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it).
- `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job: no dependency is added.
- No product file changes, so no smoke beyond the operator pass's harness boot.

**Bounds.** Every test start runs under a test-owned home. Every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint; the
rehearsals wait on the rig's exit under its `--deadline`. The live starts run under the rig's private scratch and
config; `--deadline 300` bounds each under its entry's `timeout`. The non-priming probes of each live leg are the round
entries ahead of it. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card.

**No remove-the-guard control** is planned: the chunk adds no product guard. The arm's `lost` and `unread` words are
made to fail by the pure cases of step 3 (entry 3), which produce each word from synthetic attribute words before any
graded use.

**The live atoms' must-pass readings** (validation check 4 (9)). The `KR` summary keys the live entries assert are
this chunk's own print site (step 4), so each word is read printed before any graded use, in block order:
- entry 3 runs the pure cases of step 3, which produce `kept`, `lost`, `unread` and the three readings;

- entry 4 runs the rehearsals of step 6, which print the arm's own keys (`arm: kr`, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `control:
  told-apart`, `rounds: 12`, `kr-reading: kept`) and the rig's teardown keys over the fake agent.

`kr-reading` on a real CLI is the reading itself, asserted only by the round's reading entries 18–19 (`inputs#I2`
item 4 names the predicate).

body:
- (tests) The rig's inline cases pass, every `kr_round_word` and `kr_reading` word produced from synthetic attribute
  words, the grant's `resize` word and the model's resize among them — entry `cargo nextest run -p viola-e2e --lib
  --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/^rig::/)'`.

- (tests) Both `KR` rehearsals pass over the fake agent — entry `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --integration --filter
  'test(/rig_rehearsal_kr/)'`:
  - the whole one reads `keys: x 13, del 13`, `kr-reading: kept`, and both sizes on the fake's `size` receipts;
  - the one without `resize` types nothing.

- (security) Each live start types exactly 13 `x` and 13 DEL into its own pty and resizes only its own pty, under
  `--grant box,resize`, with no prompt sent. Its summary and ledger hold closed words and counts only. Its frames stay
  under the gitignored `target/live-rig/`, and the evidence written from typed fields reads `hygiene: clean`.
  Per `security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty`, `decision/live-session-screens-kept-local`, the `KR`
  sibling of `decision/live-rig-hb-arm-keeps-attributes-only`; entries `… live KR …`, `… live KR8 …` and
  `python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/gate.py hygiene`.

- (e2e, matrix#v2-27) **On Linux, real `claude` 2.1.330 and 2.1.328 keep a key typed right after a resize.** Each
  runs unwrapped in the live rig's own pty under its scratch home. After each of 12 resizes alternating 210×45 ↔
  180×40, one `x` typed 0, 20 or 100 ms after the resize returned reads `kept` (the box row's attribute word equal to
  the no-resize control's typed word) in 12 of 12 rounds per version: `KR kr-reading=kept` and `KR8 kr-reading=kept`,
  the round's reading entries. The readings are recorded as closed words in
  `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize/evidence/live-round.md`. Any `lost` reading goes to the
  driver-paste fix as a plan revision (`inputs#I2` item 4).

- (security) The kept rig products and the live home's stamp read the same before and after the round — entries
  `… echo 'kept-products: unchanged'` and `… echo 'live-stamp: unmoved'`.

- (tests) The whole integration layer, `pre-push` and CI on HEAD read green — entries `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run
  --integration`, `bash scripts/agent-run.sh pre-push`, `python -X utf8
  ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800`.

- **Answers:** `inputs#I2` items 1–10 (the operator's K1–K4, the overseer's technical answers); `inputs#I1` (the phase
  directive).

- **Research files inspected:** `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs`, `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`,
  `src/run/gate.rs`, `src/run/send.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`,
  `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/ledger.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`, `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`.
- **(B) no start** — declined by the operator (`inputs#I2` item 1): the entry and `v2-27` say «measured».

- **(C) a wrapped arm through `viola run`** — declined: viola's 250 ms poll puts the key before the child's resize in
  most rounds, and every typed `x` moves the wheel.

- **A 30th relied ledger row with a verify probe** — not built: no send relies on the shape (`architecture ·
  decision/no-probe-for-unrelied-shapes`), and verify would type keys after a resize into every stamped CLI.

- **Paste rounds after the resize** — not built: a new key class for the grant, beyond the operator's ratification
  (`inputs#I2` item 3, «nothing wider»).

- **F1 / F2 / F3 now** — not planned: a fix is planned only after a `lost` reading, as a plan revision on the
  operator's word (`inputs#I2` item 4). F2 stands against `architecture · decision/unconfirmed-delivery-not-delivered`
  («never retried blindly»).

- **Holding or delaying a human key behind a resize** — never: `architecture · decision/human-key-never-held-behind-resize`
  («viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize»), `a11y-plan ·
  decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked`.

- **No product file, no `viola-pty` edit** — so the `CHILD_WITHIN` comment carry stays unreworded and the paste's
  `write_all` stays untouched.

- **No kept frame read into a message, log, the evidence or the tree** — the evidence is written from the ledger's
  typed fields only (`inputs#I2` item 6).
- **Never re-fire a red live entry for a green** — a `lost` is never a spare's (`inputs#I2` items 2, 7).

- **What a kept frame can hold of the operator's** (`inputs#I2` item 6). The CLI's own banner (its version, a model
  word, possibly his plan or account word), the scratch cwd's path under his home directory, and the footer hints; no
  status line, since the seed sets none. The frames are 0600 under the gitignored `target/live-rig/<run>/screens/`. No
  frame is read into a message, a log, the evidence or the tree, and the summary holds attribute words, counts and
  delays only.

- **The delay is pumped, not slept.** Each round's 0 / 20 / 100 ms after the resize runs the session's own pump for
  that span (`Session::pump`, `mod.rs` beside `settle` at `:914`), so the child's redraw output is read into the model
  while the delay passes. 0 ms means the `x` is written right after `resize` returned.

- **The keys are checked on the frame before the resize.** After a resize the rig's model keeps its cells
  (`set_size`), but a real CLI redraws. The `x` is admitted on the reading taken before the resize (the box up and
  empty), which is what `inputs#I2` item 3 ratified («each `x` only into a box read empty»). A DEL follows its `x`'s
  reading.

- **The re-read before `lost`.** A first read equal to the hint word settles once more (the rig's `QUIET` 400 ms,
  `mod.rs:45`, bounded by `--settle 10`) and reads again, so a key the CLI draws late reads `kept`.

- **The carries:**
  - `cry-7mgt7ybs` (the paste's missing time bound) and `cry-m267ghbx` (the `CHILD_WITHIN` comment) re-pin whole at
    the wrap: no step touches `crates/viola-pty`.
  - `cry-lqe3bfwx` retires as met in `1b22388f`: the 0x7f arm of `plain()` at `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs:74-85`,
    held by `rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del` (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs:417`).
  - `cry-teayoana` is the Epoch 4 boundary's.
  - `cry-234cbfoa` is acted on only at its next red met during this chunk (the `R1` rehearsal runs inside entry 22's
    whole layer); not met → re-pinned whole.

- **Counts and their basis.** 13 `x` and 13 DEL = 1 control + `KR_ROUNDS` 12 (step 3). The 22 resize call sites and the
  absence of any rig resize are from research «Graph impact» (query 1 of `tree-query-2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize.json`)
  and «Sweeps» (`grep -n "resize(" crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/*.rs` → 0).

- **Expected amendments (wrap)** — each by NAME, none folded into a class (`inputs#I2` item 3):
  - security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty — the grant gains the `KR` arm's resize of its own pty and up
    to 13 `x` and 13 DEL per start, each `x` checked on a box read empty before its resize; the operator's own answer
    K3.
  - security-plan · a new row beside decision/live-rig-hb-arm-keeps-attributes-only — «the live rig's `KR` arm resizes
    its own unwrapped pty 12 times and types one `x` and one DEL after each, before any send, and records only cell
    attributes, counts and delays»; the operator's own answer K3.
  - a11y-plan · decision/no-screen-content-parsing — the except names `KR`: box-row cell attributes after a resize of
    the rig's own pty; the operator's own answer K3.
  - test-plan · decision/no-child-screen-assertions — the same except names `KR`; the operator's own answer K3.
  - test-plan · decision/key-after-resize-waits-for-size — the except names the `KR` rehearsal beside the `hold`
    sibling; the operator's own answer K3.
  - matrix#v2-27 notes — the two readings in closed words, with the run ids of the ledger; claimed at P5.

- **The leaves the wrap re-words with the reading** (not masters): `.claude/docs/gotchas.md` H2 «the product window»
  (`:109`), `.claude/docs/services/viola-pty.md` OPEN (`:31`).

- **No row NOT in the P3 block's §4 is reached by this plan** (checked against the seven rows files and the history
  files at P4: the plan's touchpoints are the five `viola-e2e` files of research's list); `inputs#I2` item 9.

- **Expected amendments (wrap)** — each by NAME, none folded into a class (`inputs#I2` item 3). Each is a boundary
  widening the operator answered himself, to the P3 block's fork K3, given before the wrap (`inputs#I2` item 3, his
  words relayed verbatim by the overseer). Pattern: the playbook's `rul-bznresq5` («Boundary widening the founder
  answered himself»), so the wrap halts once on ONE answer card citing that record.
  - security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty — the grant gains the `KR` arm's resize of its own pty and up
    to 13 `x` and 13 DEL per start, each `x` checked on a box read empty before its resize.
  - security-plan · a new row beside decision/live-rig-hb-arm-keeps-attributes-only — «the live rig's `KR` arm resizes
    its own unwrapped pty 12 times and types one `x` and one DEL after each, before any send, and records only cell
    attributes, counts and delays».
  - a11y-plan · decision/no-screen-content-parsing — the except names `KR`: box-row cell attributes after a resize of
    the rig's own pty.
  - test-plan · decision/no-child-screen-assertions — the same except names `KR`.
  - test-plan · decision/key-after-resize-waits-for-size — the except names the `KR` rehearsal beside the `hold`
    sibling.

- **The readings reach the ledger through the claim** (P5 step 4): `v2-27`'s ref is written by implement on green,

body:
# Implement directive — «Key after a resize» (chunk 2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize)

The plan is approved (P5 card 1, plan rev 3). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents from the store and
its evidence dir from disk first. This directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. Nothing a kept frame holds
is quoted, described or summarised in a message — closed words, counts and delays only. This session is driven
through the pinned product, which holds none of the last seven mends: call no scheduled-wake or timer tool.

## The live cap for THIS chunk (the operator's own answers, read 2026-11-22; nothing widens it)

- **TWO base starts and ONE spare on one ledger, through the rig's new `KR` arm: `KR` (2.1.330, `--cap 1`) and
  `KR8` (2.1.328 by path, `--cap 2`).** Each: one real `claude` UNWRAPPED in the rig's own pty, a scratch folder
  and a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, his real HOME the process's home as every earlier unwrapped rig start; no
  prompt sent; up to 13 `x` and 13 DEL and 12 resizes of the rig's own pty, each `x` only into a box read empty,
  NEVER into a dialog — a modal or a wrong first screen stops the start; the stop is the rig's own Ctrl-C.
- **A `lost` reading is a red that is NOT retried and NOT a spare's.** Both starts run (each version's reading is
  its own); after the round, any `lost` stops implement before the report's green path, with the summaries'
  closed words (`kept` · `lost` · `unread` counts, `lost-at`): the fix is a plan revision that goes back to the
  operator. The spare is spent only on the overseer's word, for a start that read `refused shape` or
  `confounded`, or was cut by the token window or a host stall.
- **Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once per
  start by the rig (a 0600 copy, removed on every exit path); `~/.claude.json` is searched for the rig's own
  needles only after a moved stamp. `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` is read for its sha alone, right before the
  round, and must read unmoved after it. The frames stay under `target/live-rig/`, 0600, and never land.
- Each start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made.

## The host

- Run nothing heavier than this chunk's own gate entries. Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole.
- **Before the round: STOP and say in one line that the round is ready** (the rig cases and the `KR` rehearsals
  green). The overseer arranges a quiet host window and sends the word to go on, with the time to read hostwatch
  FROM. A CONTENDED reading that names a NEIGHBOUR makes no start: stop and say so.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.

## Stops

- **The plan's order is the order.** The arm, its pure cases and its rehearsals over the fake agent green before
  the round; the round as ONE call.
- An after-read that does not hold (a kept product or the live stamp moved) stops before the operator pass.
- A red that would move a plan entry stops implement before the operator pass: say which entry and why.
- The carried rehearsal red (`rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del`) is acted on only at its next
  red: the printed rig summary and the kept frame read and the cause named BEFORE any mend; no retry, no
  loosened entry. A CI red on it is recorded and NOT re-run before the overseer's word.
- No product file changes in this run: a need to touch one stops implement and is said.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone by a recursive delete: name it in the report.
- Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home; no test starts a real `claude`. No leaf gains a figure the
  code states. No master row is reworded in this skill. No `matrix#v2-27 notes` line is written from the plan's
  prose (the audit's misread you named).

## On green (both starts `kept`)

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.
End every process you start.

# The operator's answer after the cut `KR8` — «Key after a resize»: a plan REVISION

Read at 2026-11-22T08:32:19Z, his dialog in the overseer's session, after the round of 2026-11-22T08:26:30Z (`KR` kept 12/12;
`KR8` 7 of 7 kept, stopped `dirty-box: 8`, `unverified`). This relay, `relay-resize-p3.md` and the phase directive
are the only files of this folder you read or snap. It goes with a plan REVISION through the phase's door, in a
NEW phase run, in a fresh window: read the chunk's documents, its evidence dir and the stopped run's outcome from
disk first. No live start in the revision; no scheduled-wake or timer tool; no compiled screen literal and
nothing of a kept frame printed in chat.

## The operator's own word

1. **«Починить риг, затем запасной (Recommended)».** The rig's settle is mended through a revision (the rig's
   test crate only, no product file), THEN the spare is spent on `KR8-2`: 2.1.328 by path, the same shape as
   `KR8` (up to 13 `x`, 13 DEL, 12 resizes of the rig's own pty, never into a dialog), `--cap 2 --spare 1` on the
   same ledger — the spare line, not a third base start. He was shown: that the cause is a READING of the rig's
   timings, not measured (the settle counted quiet from a byte received before the key, the box read 50 ms after
   the DEL); that a CLI that truly did not take the DEL cannot be ruled out, no later frame standing; and that
   if `KR8-2` again gives no reading, no start follows without him. `KR`'s reading stands as taken.

## Technical (the overseer's)

2. **The settle after a key waits for a byte that arrives AFTER that key** (the rig's own clock at the write),
   bounded as today; say the line it changes and every arm that shares the function (HB and the earlier arms

data.head: ### B. Revision 1 — the rig's settle mended (`inputs#I6` items 2–5; the rig's test crate only)

body:
7. **The after-key settle** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`, beside `Session::settle`:
   - A pure predicate `settled_after(last_byte, mark, now, quiet) -> bool` (no clock read of its own): true only when
     `mark` is `None` or the last drained byte is LATER than `mark`, and `now − last_byte ≥ quiet`.
   - A new `Session::settle_since(mark: Option<Instant>, until, bound) -> bool`: the same 50 ms pump loop as `settle`,
     met when `settled_after(…, self.quiet)` holds and `until` admits the reading; ended as `settle` ends (the child
     exited while quiet, `bound`, a stop requested); its elapsed time pushed to `settles` (so `settle-ms` keeps every
     KR settle, the re-read's included).
   - `Session` gains `quiet: Duration`, set from the plan (step 10), `QUIET` (400 ms) by default.
   - **The mark** is the rig's own clock at the write: before each KR key, the session drains what is already queued
     (`pump(Duration::ZERO)`), the mark is taken, then `type_key` writes. Named residual: a byte the child wrote
     before the key but which reached the reader thread's channel between that drain and the write reads as after
     the key — a window of the drain-to-write gap alone.
   - **`Session::settle` (`mod.rs:958-975`) is not changed — no line of it.** Every other arm keeps calling it: the
     21 call sites (`grep -n "\.settle(\|hint_cell_attrs(" crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs | wc -l`) less the KR ones
     below, `first_frame` (`:1462`, shared with `HB` and every arm that reads a first frame), `hint_cell_attrs`
     (`HB`, `CC`), the trust pass's `TrustDriver::settle_after` (`:1500`) and the wrapped arms. So `HB` and the
     earlier arms' readings do not move by construction; the cases that hold them run whole in entry 5
     (`binary(rig_rehearsal)`): among them `rig_rehearsal_hb_reads_the_fresh_box_then_x_and_del_with_no_send`,
     `rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del`, `rig_rehearsal_cc_confirms_context_under_the_kept_stamp`.
   - **The KR lines it changes:** `kr_control_round`'s two after-key settles (`:2382`, `:2387`), its box settle
     (`:2379`), and in `kr_rounds` the box settle (`:2403`), the x settle (`:2422`), the `again` re-read's pump and
     settle (`:2426-2427`, now `pump_for(self.quiet)` then `settle_since(None, …)`) and the DEL settle (`:2435`). The
     two key settles take the key's mark; the box settles and the re-reads take `None`. `first_frame` stays `settle`.
   - Inline cases: `a_byte_drained_before_the_key_never_settles_it` (a last byte before the mark, however long the
     quiet: false); `a_byte_after_the_key_settles_once_quiet` (after the mark: false before `quiet`, true at it);
     `no_mark_settles_on_quiet_alone` (today's rule).

8. **A dirty box told apart from a late redraw** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`:
   - A pure `kr_box_word(hint, first, again: Option<&str>) -> &'static str`: `clean` when `first` equals `hint`;
     `late-redraw` when `first` does not and `again` does; else `dirty`.
   - In `kr_rounds` step 1: the box read up (`settle_since(None, Reading::is_box_up, …)`) and its `box_attr` read.
     Not the hint word → ONE re-read: `pump_for(self.quiet)`, `settle_since(None, Reading::is_box_up, …)`,
     `box_attr` again. `late-redraw` → the tally counts it and the round goes on, its keys checked on that re-read
     frame; `dirty` → `dirty-box` at round n, and the arm stops (as today).
   - `KrTally` gains `late_redraws`; `KrTally::put` adds the summary key `late-redraw` (the count, `0` when none) —
     a READING, never an atom (verification-harness.md 2026-11-19). `dirty-box` reads the round only when the
     re-read was still dirty.
   - `finish`'s whole-start rule is unchanged: a still-dirty box stops the start with `rounds` < 12, `unverified`.
   - Inline cases: `the_kr_box_word_tells_a_late_redraw_from_a_dirty_box` (all three words);
     `the_kr_tally_puts_its_closed_words_and_the_whole_start_rule_reads_them` gains `late-redraw: 0` and a tally with
     one late redraw reading `late-redraw: 1` and `dirty-box: none`.

9. **The rehearse-only seams** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` (`Plan` and `arm_kr`) and
   `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` (`Verb::Rehearse`). The fake agent draws every key at once and is
   not changed: it is a root-package file outside the rig's test crate (`inputs#I6` item 1, «the rig's test crate
   only»). The new words are rehearsed by **«its like» — two rig-side stand-ins over the plain fake** (`inputs#I6`
   item 5, «say which»):
   - `--kr-del-seam withheld:<n>` (n 1–11): round n types no DEL after its `x`, so the box keeps it, as a CLI that
     never draws the DEL. Round n+1 reads dirty on both reads.
   - `--kr-del-seam late:<n>` (n 1–11): round n types no DEL after its `x`; round n+1's first box read is dirty, the
     rig types that DEL then (drain, mark, `settle_since(Some(mark), …)`), and the re-read reads clean, as a DEL whose
     redraw came late.
   - `--quiet-ms <100–400>` sets `Session::quiet` (step 7) for the start.
   - All three are fields of `Verb::Rehearse` only, accepted with the `kr` arm alone (any other arm: `refused: usage`,
     exit 2, as `--contain` with any arm but `sf`). `live` has no such field, so a live start carrying one is a clap
     error: `refused: usage`, exit 2, before any ledger line. A `KrSeam::parse` refuses any other form (`late:0`,
     `late:12`, `x:3`, a bare word).
   - Inline cases: `the_kr_seam_reads_withheld_and_late_rounds_and_refuses_any_other_form`; the quiet bound
     (`100` and `400` read, `99` and `401` refused).

10. **The CLI doc lines** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`: the module doc names the three `kr`-only
    rehearse options in one sentence, and that `live` takes none.

11. **The rehearsals** — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`, over the fake agent (`case.child(true, &[])`):
    - `rig_rehearsal_kr_reads_each_key_kept_after_its_own_resize` passes `--quiet-ms 100` and asserts
      `late-redraw: 0` beside its keys today (exit 0, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `rounds: 12`, `kr-reading: kept`,
      `dirty-box: none`).
    - New `rig_rehearsal_kr_reads_a_late_redraw_and_keeps_the_round` (`--quiet-ms 100 --kr-del-seam late:3`): exit 0,
      `keys: x 13, del 13`, `rounds: 12`, `kept: 12/12`, `late-redraw: 1`, `dirty-box: none`, `kr-reading: kept`,
      torn down.
    - New `rig_rehearsal_kr_stops_on_a_box_still_dirty_on_its_re_read` (`--quiet-ms 100 --kr-del-seam withheld:2`):
      exit 1, `keys: x 3, del 2`, `rounds: 2`, `dirty-box: 3`, `late-redraw: 0`, `kr-reading: unverified`, torn
      down.
    - New `rig_rehearsal_kr_seams_refuse_a_live_start_and_another_arm`: `live KR8-2 … --quiet-ms 100` and `live
      KR8-2 … --kr-del-seam late:3` (each `--ledger` in the case's own dir) and `rehearse hb … --kr-del-seam late:3`
      each exit 2 with `refused: usage`, the case's ledger absent, nothing spawned (`assert_torn_down`). The two
      `live` spawns keep `CI=1` set and name a `--cli` no install holds, so even a parse that took the option would
      refuse before any start: the case can never reach a real CLI.
    - Keys are read from the rig's own `keys` word, never from the receipt (`test-plan ·
      decision/rig-no-key-read-from-keys-word`).

12. **The rehearsal's margin** (`inputs#I6` item 5). The late-redraw rehearsal adds a re-read to a 12-round start, so a
    rehearsal round lengthens by construction, at the 12.4 s the stopped run measured against `--deadline 15` and
    `WITHIN` 18 s (the outcome's «Deviations»). The mend is `--quiet-ms 100` on the three whole `kr` rehearsals: the
    rig's own 400 ms `QUIET` is the larger share of each of the ~37 settles of a whole start. No bound moves
    (`WITHIN` 18 s, `--deadline 15`, the 20 s lint). Predicted under 10 s each — implement records what entry 4's
    log measures for each `kr` rehearsal (nextest's per-test time) in `evidence/live-round.md`; a reading at 13 s or
    more stops implement for the operator (no bound is raised to pass it).

- **Mending the shared `Session::settle`** — rejected: every other arm, `HB` among them, would read under a new rule
  (`inputs#I6` item 2, «HB and the earlier arms must not change their readings»); the mend is a KR-only method.

- **Raising `--deadline`, `WITHIN` or the 20 s lint for the margin** — rejected: the margin is won by the rehearsal's
  `--quiet-ms 100`, never by moving a bound (`inputs#I6` item 5).

- **A third base start, a re-fire of `KR` or `KR8`, a retry after a still-dirty box** — never (`inputs#I6` items 1,
  4): `KR8-2` is the spare line; a start after it is the operator's.

- **The delay is pumped, not slept** (`Session::pump_for`): the child's redraw output is read into the model while the
  delay passes; 0 ms means the `x` is written right after `resize` returned.

- **The keys are checked on the frame before the resize** (`inputs#I2` item 3, «each `x` only into a box read
  empty»), or on the clean re-read frame after a late redraw (step 8); a DEL follows its `x`'s reading.

- **What the mend changes in a reading, by construction.** A key whose echo comes within the first 50 ms pump read
  the same before; one whose echo comes later is now waited for instead of read early. A key that draws nothing (a DEL
  into a box the CLI already emptied) waits the `--settle` bound and is read then. So `KR`'s `kept` reading on
  2.1.330, taken under the old settle, is not re-taken: the old rule could read a late `x` echo only as `kept` (the
  `again` re-read) or as `lost`/`unread`, never a false `kept` (`kr_round_word` reads `kept` only on the typed word).

- **`cry-234cbfoa`** (the intermittent `rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del` red, an `HB`-shaped read
  after a DEL) may share this mechanism — a HYPOTHESIS, not read. Its own rule stands: acted on only at its next red
  met during this chunk (entries 5 and 23 run it), read from its kept frame; not met → re-pinned whole, the hypothesis
  named beside it at the wrap.

- **Counts and their basis.** 13 `x` and 13 DEL = 1 control + `KR_ROUNDS` 12 (step 3). The withheld rehearsal's
  `keys: x 3, del 2` = 1 control pair + rounds 1–2's `x` + round 1's DEL (round 2's withheld), `rounds: 2`, then round

  | wc -l` at HEAD's tree with the stopped run's edits. The ~37 settles of a whole KR start: 1 first frame + 3 control +
  3 × 12 rounds (box, `x`, DEL), from the stopped run's `settle-ms` (26 values over 7 rounds and a stop).

- **Expected amendments (wrap)** — each by NAME, none folded into a class (`inputs#I2` item 3):
  - the take-up's five, standing: security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty (the `KR` resize and up to 13
    `x` and 13 DEL per start); a new security-plan row beside decision/live-rig-hb-arm-keeps-attributes-only (the `KR`
    arm's resizes, keys, attributes, counts and delays); a11y-plan · decision/no-screen-content-parsing and test-plan ·

  code states. No master row is reworded in this skill. No `matrix#v2-27 notes` line is written from the plan's

`/context` writes its stdout tag to the transcript and submits no prompt within the confirmation window) · `trust-record` (probed by `viola verify`'s Run F, after Run E: passes only when the trust record was written, Run A showed the trust modal, and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box) · `browser-tools-prompt` (relied; `pass` when some verify run's first screen is the CLI's browser-tools prompt, `absent` when no run met it, `fail` when any first screen reads none; the one relied row whose `absent` counts toward verified) · `identity-floor` (relied; passes when every CLAUDE name the CLI adds to a SessionStart hook is an identity-floor name or a known non-identity name, fails on an unknown name or an unread or off-shape env-names file, kept names dropped before the check; its probe stamped as `measured.env_probe`, names only) · `cross-session-prefix` (relied; passes only when a print-mode sender's message to Run B (the sender addressing Run B by its inbox socket address `uds:<runtime>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock`, composed from the runtime dir and Run B's pid, never by a bare session id), Run B started with the crossSessionInbound accept settings, arrives opening with the CLI's cross-session harness prefix, else fails, never on the sender's words; no runtime dir runs no turn; its probe stamped as `measured.cross_session_probe`, closed words and one number); the relied set `LedgerRow::relied()` (every row of `ALL`, in its order); (no status-line capture, variant or shell verdict: viola intercepts no status line); `resume_target` (Run E's target id: the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, only when `is_session_id` accepts it) and `resume_variants` (`SessionStart.resume-1.json`); `AgentsCapture` / `agents_variant` (Run B's agents capture and its `Agents.recorded-1.json` filter); `TypedRun`, `Probes { print, typed, trusted, dialogs, resumed, agents }` (`trusted`: Run B's captures in claim order; `resumed`: Run E's captures in claim order; `agents`: Run B's one agents capture, an `AgentsCapture`, on which `agents-join` passes only when it parses and holds exactly one row whose `pid` is Run B's child pid, whose `sessionId` is the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture and whose status is idle or busy (`agents_joined`), and fails with no capture; under a 24×1 PTY that panics vt100's feed), `--start-screen <phase>` (under `--screens`, a trusted start draws `Screen.<phase>` in place of its ready screen and keeps it standing; each stdin byte is one `key` receipt line, Ctrl-C ends it with no key line, and no byte reaches the input box). `--transcript` (argv-only) creates `<exe dir>/transcripts/` at 0700 at start and gives the launch SessionStart a `transcript_path` to a seeded 0600 file named by its session id (replayed framing variants not rewritten; a test that must have no transcript removes none from the shared build, it runs its own private copy of the fake agent in a test-owned directory); under `--local-command-mode` a submitted local command whose post-condition is the stdout tag, and under `--framing` the exact verify echo probe command or the exact `/context` probe command, append one stdout tag line to the last started session's transcript and fire no hook. `--settings <file>` is accepted; the fake agent reads its cross-session inbox only when the value holds the accept settings, and otherwise ignores it (its cross-session sender resolves its target by the uds socket address alone, delivers only to its sibling and refuses an address not of the uds shape). Beside `--turn-stop`, `--turn-fail <variant>` ends the turn with the recorded set's `StopFailure.<variant>` payload in place of `Stop.default`. `--trust-config <file>` reads trust from that config file by the CLI's walk (the canonical cwd's exact key, then each parent up to the git root, so inside a repository the cwd's own record counts) through a bounded read; any failure reads untrusted. Under `--screens` with an untrusted cwd it draws claude 2.1.325's unnumbered trust form over the set's recorded modal (selector first on No, directly above the recorded trust row, row 16 with no recorded modal); arrows move the selector, Enter on No exits 1, and the launch SessionStart fires only after Enter on the trust row, which draws the ready screen. Built for `viola revive`'s tests and, under the fake agent, verify's Run E: `--resume <id>` (the launch SessionStart reports source `resume` and that id) and `--fork-session` (beside `--resume`, the compiled fork id; alone it changes nothing); and the capped test-only hold `--stop-receipt-hold-ms` (1 000 ms at most, holding the Stop hook's receipt to force a race window open), and the test-only hold `--trust-record-blank` (a start trusted by the trust record alone draws no screen, holding verify's Run F window open for a stop case). Built: the mode word `agents` (a first word `agents` answers `agents --json` from files beside its exe: `agents-mode` (`recorded` · `oversize` · `malformed`, absent = `recorded`), `agents-rows.json` (planted rows) and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry, a row written just before its launch SessionStart fires, a dead or reused pid skipped through one `viola_state::liveness::start_times()` read; built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`; no option and no env added). Exits on `\x03` or at stdin EOF, and exits 1 on Enter on the trust form's No, first waiting for a hook still running and starting no other; on Unix every command it spawns (each hook) runs in a process group of its own (`process_group(0)`, as the `--exit-no-eof` holder does), because a hangup of its PTY's foreground group, at its exit as session leader or when a killed wrapper closes the PTY, cuts a `viola hook` short in its exit-time coverage write (a cut-short profile, measured); the agent itself, its PTY's session leader, cannot leave that group (`setpgid` refuses a leader), so on Unix its exit ignores SIGHUP from its first step (`\x03` or stdin's end): a hangup that lands while it exits (a killed wrapper, or portable-pty's SIGHUP-first kill) no longer cuts its own exit-time coverage write, and one that lands before the exit begins still ends it (measured). That exit, shared Unix code, is witnessed on Linux only: `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` `fake_agent_exit_outlives_a_hangup_that_lands_while_it_exits` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`) reads the SIGHUP disposition through `ps -o sigignore= -p <pid>`; it runs on CI's one leg, `ubuntu-latest`.

- The hidden capture arm, `hook <event> --capture`, does no obs init and writes no line (a bounded panic-line exemption, obs-plan §10). `viola verify` runs `strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens: a refused tree is exit 1 with the home pair, no step line, no log and no line; a refused `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`, nothing read or written) prints the same pair and exits 1 through its own `process-exit`, which under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` carries `detail:"strict-modes-failed"`; every other refusal past the tree check writes its own code there (`program-not-found`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `version-unreadable`, `unclean-fixture`), a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and the fixture's `<file>` enters no code. `viola verify`'s trust-record write and removal emit no log line and no span (a refused symlinked, non-regular or foreign file included); the outcome rides only the stamps. The reading of the CLI's browser-tools prompt as a modal adds no log line, span, event or detail code of its own; verify's reading of it (its `absent` step word included) reaches only the ledger stamp and verify's stdout, whose one fixed line on a met prompt is the only record that the prompt stood at start. Each wrapped start of `viola run` and `viola revive` on a verified CLI opens no span for its trust step and writes exactly one INFO `trust-record` line to the run role file, its required `detail` one of a closed set of 16 start words (`trust-record` in the event enum of both the diag-line and the detail-line schema), and the word never refuses the start; no path, key or value of the claude config reaches any line, stamp or summary. A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) starts no further spawn, kills and reaps the child it is running, closes every spawn pair it opened (a child of an interactive PTY run killed at the stop closes with `duration_ms` and a `child_exit_status`, the PTY pump's exit code; every other spawn pair it started closes with `child_exit_status` and `duration_ms` as well, and a stopped run writes only the pairs it started) and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` (a member of the `process-exit` `detail` enum `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes); `run`'s version gate observes no stop, save during the start's automatic verify: a SIGINT or SIGTERM there TERMs the verify child, KILLs it after a 30 s grace, writes the `auto-verify` `process-exit`, then re-raises the signal, the start ending with no `process-exit` of its own, no stamp, no snapshot and no session.

- Run start's span chain is `run.start` (INTERNAL, root) › `state.snapshot_recover` › `run.collision_check` › `run.pin_copy` › `run.version_gate` › `channel.bind` › `state.snapshot_write` › `state.heartbeat_start` › `pty.spawn` (CLIENT), with no budget span. A `release` whose `from` is not a string or that carries any budget key (true, false, a string or null) is a plain `-32602` (data null) after the release-from-driver check, with no `release-from-driver` line, no wheel moved and no record; its `channel-response` carries `detail` `invalid-params` on both sides at WARN. The implicit link record on a `send` or an `answer`, the explicit `link` / `unlink` methods the driven wrapper serves (their trace the call's `channel-request` / `channel-response` pair, which holds neither name), the link set's restore at start and the replay's link rule carry no span and no process-log line of their own; `driver`, `driven` and `since` reach no home-level line. The wrapper's stdin typed mark and its held scheduled-wakes count are in-memory state that open no span and write no line of their own, and carry no key and no prompt text. The send's transcript echo read (the end offset before the paste and the tag count after it) opens no span and writes no line or span field of its own; its result shows only as the `send-confirmed` line inside `run.confirm_window`. A `send-refused` line carries `refusal`, `detail`, `side` and `wheel`, never `window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at` or `paused`. At a dialog hold's end (`run.dialog_await`'s `deadline_ms`, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` in ms, 60 000–3 600 000, default 60 000) the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` product line and writes one `dialog-answered{corr:<dialog_id>, dialog_kind, deadline_hit:true, duration_ms}` with no `from` / `from_trust`; a hand-back or an answer writes neither; the hook then writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s).

record.title: A key typed right after a resize
record.requirement: whether real `claude` on Linux loses a key typed right after a terminal resize is measured, and fixed if it does
record.observed_gap: Whether real claude loses a key typed right after a terminal resize is unmeasured on Linux, and the fleet's window placement resizes neighbouring windows (res-wqnre2ex).

verification.acceptance: On Linux, real `claude` 2.1.330 and 2.1.328 each run unwrapped in the live rig's own pty under its scratch home. After each of 12 resizes alternating 210×45 ↔ 180×40, one `x` typed 0, 20 or 100 ms after the resize returned reads `kept` (the box row's attribute word equal to the no-resize control's typed word) in 12 of 12 rounds per version: `KR kr-reading=kept` (2.1.330, the round of 2026-11-22T08:26:30Z, as it stands) and `KR8-2 kr-reading=kept` (2.1.328, the spare, after the rig's after-key settle waits for a byte drained after its key and a dirty box is re-read once); `KR8` (2.1.328) read 7 of 7 rounds kept and was cut at round 8 by the rig's settle, `unverified`, recorded as read. The readings are recorded as closed words in the chunk's evidence, and the arm's rehearsals over the fake agent hold the mechanics in CI, the late-redraw and still-dirty words included. Any `lost` reading takes the fix half to the driver's paste (a resize polled between the gate's ready and the paste sends the send back into the gate; human keys never held), as a plan revision on the operator's word, the human-key loss recorded as the CLI's.
verification.ref: live rig `viola-live-rig live KR` (2.1.330, kr-reading=kept 12/12, 2026-11-22T08:26:30Z) and `live KR8-2` (2.1.328, kr-reading=kept 12/12, 2026-11-22T09:18:17Z), read back by the round's reading entries into .andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize/evidence/live-round.md; mechanics: crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs::rig_rehearsal_kr_reads_each_key_kept_after_its_own_resize, ::rig_rehearsal_kr_reads_a_late_redraw_and_keeps_the_round, ::rig_rehearsal_kr_stops_on_a_box_still_dirty_on_its_re_read
